lead.headline: Investors doubt Anthropic can price IPO at $1.5 trillion
lead.summary: Investors told CNBC that even a $1.5 trillion valuation for Anthropic's IPO is now in doubt after this week's tech selloff, with one calling it a "stretch." Anthropic had been looking toward $2 trillion until recently and was privately valued at $965 billion in May. One investor said $1 trillion to $1.25 trillion is a more likely target. Anthropic declined to comment. It plans to list on the Nasdaq under the ticker ANT and is expected to start its roadshow next week.

main.headline: OpenAI raises $11 billion at $1.25 trillion valuation
main.summary: OpenAI has received about $11 billion in the first tranche of a funding round that values it at $1.25 trillion, Bloomberg reports. The full round could reach $20 billion, with the rest expected in coming weeks, according to The Decoder. OpenAI originally sought $30 billion at a $1.4 trillion valuation, The Decoder reports. Investors include Coatue Management, T. Rowe Price, SoftBank, Sequoia Capital, Founders Fund, Andreessen Horowitz and a United Arab Emirates consortium.

main.headline: House chairs ask Nvidia's Huang to brief them on alleged Chinese spy
main.summary: The New York Times reports that US intelligence concluded China's Ministry of State Security recruited Megaspeed executive Alice Huang to gather information on Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. The Times also reports that officials did not believe Jensen Huang knew of this, and that neither has been charged. Three House committee chairs have asked him to attend a closed-door briefing on his interactions with her, with a reply due by November 11. Nvidia did not say whether he will attend.

main.headline: METR finds Anthropic's model progress has roughly doubled in pace
main.summary: The nonprofit METR, after eleven weeks of access to Anthropic's internal data, says Anthropic's model test scores have risen about 1.9 times faster since October 2025. It estimates about 80% of the speedup comes from AI use in Anthropic's own research. Anthropic redacted most of the evidence METR rated most informative, according to METR. METR says the warning level in Anthropic's Responsible Scaling Policy may have been reached on July 15, and that Anthropic's public risk report understated the acceleration.

main.headline: Ex-OpenAI engineer pleads not guilty to bugging company headquarters
main.summary: Abdulrahman Alfozan, a Saudi national, pleaded not guilty in San Francisco federal court to one count of interception of oral communications. Prosecutors say he placed a recording device in a television in an OpenAI executive conference room on Sept. 28. He has been held without bail since early October and faces up to five years in prison if convicted. His next court date is Nov. 17.

europe_brief.headline: Swedish privacy regulator opens review of Arbetsförmedlingen AI system
europe_brief.summary: The Swedish data protection authority IMY is reviewing the AI system the Public Employment Service uses to assess jobseekers for the "Rusta och matcha" program. It will examine how the system works, how personal data is handled and whether it involves automated decision-making, after tips and media reports.
